items.title: Port pickup response and electronics calculations to Rust
items.body:
The Rust pickup/electronics component now covers circuit combination, complex transfer, both peak fits, complete response tables, smoothing/float32 conversion, body pole offsets, coil placement/projection, phases and electric gain/trim primitives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Implement pickup position, normalized host-angle arithmetic, pole/coil geometry and level calculations.
- [x] Implement parallel/series/phase primitives, volume/tone resistance, capacitance, taper and load behavior.
- [x] Differentially compare response tables and complete component outputs, including internal pickup combinations and edge values.

## Validation

3,826 circuit combinations; 2,322 raw responses; 387 primary and 282 secondary fits; 900 bandpass/complex checks; 280 complete tables; 252 smoothed outputs with all 83 assigned fields; 261 pole-offset outputs; 120 projection traces; 129 bundled-model placements and 72 synthetic host cases; 216 level/trim cases. Only independently observed level fields are asserted for inactive pickups. 57 all-feature Rust tests pass, as do Clippy, fmt, release fixture tests and optimized builds.

See `docs/pickup-response.md` and `src/pickup/`. Native references use private Unicorn execution and disclosed initialized-host-libm adapters. Geometry comparisons bypass electrical fitting/final setters; projection captures setter arguments rather than testing packed words.

## Scope boundary

This completes component calculations, not the complete application or all possible inputs. Java angle/unit conversion, combination selection/stock overrides, acoustic host orchestration and final patch assembly remain #3/#4; historical runtime rounding #5; whole-engine parity #6; broader parameter-domain coverage #7. Audio rendering/sustain/bend equivalence, device firmware emulation and physical safety are unverified. Earlier uninitialized whole-generator references remain invalidated; use versioned v2 candidates.

## Hardware boundary

No live USB/MIDI/audio access, device writes, reset, preset switching or firmware installation is authorized. Keep all source hardware locks enabled with no runtime override. All validation uses files/private CPU emulation only.

## Initial DSP milestone

The recovered inventory now lists 17 blocks, 59 hardware-word procedures and shared helpers (`docs/dsp-inventory.json`). Full word ownership remains pending. `NativePatch` implements 15 scalar/control setters and the raw VX bit encoder; 1,012 arbitrary IEEE-pattern encodings and 297 seeded full-1,091-word setter comparisons match original machine code. 60 all-feature Rust tests, Clippy, fmt and release DSP tests pass. Remaining work includes coefficient/table setters, block calculations, tuning/string DSP, output-word ownership and all-block assembly. This is an offline word buffer with no upload/device API. See `docs/dsp-implementation.md`.


## Coefficient and block assembly milestone

54 of 59 hardware-word procedures now have implemented primitives and native comparisons. The scalar v2 corpus has 315 cases including six-band EQ counts; 927 table/scalar and 1,218 per-block coefficient cases compare all 1,091 seeded words. Complete pickup word assembly passes 360 geometry + 960 response cases. A further 1,008 cases cover volume, mix, decay, drone, pitch and microphone preparation/assembly at three rates. 66 Rust tests, Clippy, fmt, optimized fixtures/build pass. Body-resonance, low-cut, string EQ/tone, twelve-string EQ, sitar, reverb, pick-filter/compressor parameter math, full word ownership and all-block assembly remain pending. The native layout has intentional overlapping word ranges, retained rather than relocated. None of these tests render guitar audio or validate sustain/bend sound. See `docs/dsp-implementation.md`.


## Filter/word-map milestone

600 generic filter-helper cases and 864 low-cut/pick-filter/compressor/reverb parameter-to-word cases now pass against original instructions, with all 1091 seeded words compared. The 110-case native word trace reproduced every versioned output and maps 748 instruction-written words; 343 unobserved words stayed zero in the corpus and remain semantically unknown (not claimed reserved). See `docs/dsp-word-map.md` and JSON ranges. 69 Rust tests and debug/release/Clippy/fmt checks pass. Body resonance, string EQ/tone, twelve-string EQ, sitar and final all-block integration remain pending; rendered audio/sustain/bending remain unverified.


## Completed DSP component port

All 17 block parameter-to-word paths are now implemented. Additional original-instruction checks pass: 2,304 mixed-precision EQ coefficient cases, 432 string/twelve-string EQ block cases, 288 sitar cases (including finite zero-Q and signed zero), and 432 body/string-tone cases. Full raw-body assembly matches every one of 1,091 words for all 28 vendor bodies × six variants and eight synthetic bodies × six variants: 216 outputs total. The 48 synthetic full outputs are committed as fresh-clone fixtures; vendor assets remain private. The original constructor default rate is 39062.5 Hz (0x47189680), not a measured hardware or USB recording rate.

78 all-feature Rust tests, 24 optimized DSP tests, Clippy with warnings denied, formatting and reference checks pass. All words are indexed: 748 have observed instruction-write evidence and 343 remain explicitly semantically unknown/zero in the tested corpus. The remaining five hardware procedure entries without direct primitive comparison stay labeled; name/metadata and Java/model host orchestration belong to #4. Historical libm parity (#5), whole-engine parity (#6), model domains (#7), and rendered sustain/bend/tuning/audio behavior (#33) remain open. Hardware locks are unchanged. See docs/dsp-implementation.md.

items.title: Validate native oracle math and historical runtime rounding
items.body:
Complete native generation uses host libm adapters, which may differ from historical macOS math at quantization boundaries.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Record oracle math/runtime dependencies and floating-point control settings reproducibly.
- [x] Compare sensitive transcendental functions and conversions with an independent original-runtime reference where feasible (embedded original Windows math; historical Mac runtime still unavailable).
- [ ] Quantify and resolve output differences near quantization thresholds; document any unresolved accuracy limits.

## References

- `scripts/coefficient_oracle.py`
- `scripts/native_oracle.py`
- `docs/offline-generator-results.md`

## Hardware boundary

No USB/MIDI traffic, device writes, reset, preset switching, or firmware installation is authorized. Keep all source-level hardware locks enabled; no runtime unlock. Use local artifacts, synthetic inputs, fake transports and CPU emulation only.

## Confirmed module-initialization defect (2026-11-15)

The oracle loader did not execute Mach-O module constructors. `_kMultTone` (0x3d798) and `_kMultVolume` (0x3d7a0) remain zero; original startup initializes them through `__GLOBAL__I_kMultVolume` (0x33780). The earlier 110-case whole-generator baseline and derived JNI-output references are invalidated. Generation now rejects this incomplete runtime. Audit all 26 initializer entries and required runtime behavior, record adapters/rounding, and rebuild versioned references before using full-generator outputs. Preserve old results labeled invalidated. Independently verified body interpolation, circuit combination, raw complex transfer and primary-fit routines do not use these globals and retain their limited validation scope.


## Initialized reference follow-up

All 26 original Mach-O initializer entries now execute in private Unicorn memory. A separate startup verifier checks all 52 complex constants, 53 captured destructor registrations, fresh-state repeatability and rejection guards. The versioned initialized-host-libm-v2 sweep passes 110 complete generator cases plus four JNI/direct comparisons; 102 outputs differ from the invalidated old baseline. The first corrected sweep hit the 20M instruction cap at Chime Toaster Bridge; its failure is preserved. A targeted replay justified the bounded 200M/10s whole-generation limit; startup retains 1M/2s. See `docs/native-runtime.md`. Earlier uninitialized output references remain invalidated. Historical libm rounding, teardown, full Rust generation and audio equivalence are not established; #5 remains open.

## Offline math audit milestone (2026-11-15)

See docs/math-runtime-audit.md. Canonical Mac trace: 684,564 calls, 206,228 distinct inputs; all 110 canonical output hashes unchanged. MPFR-256/512 target rounding agrees across that trace; glibc differs by up to one ULP. MPFR-256 substitution changes four coefficient words plus checksum in one of 110 packed outputs. Recompiled Apple Libm-92 is only a source candidate: 92 of 110 packed outputs change, and special-value behavior differs; it is not authenticated historical Mac behavior.

Original embedded Windows CRT math executes in private Unicorn memory with all OS imports forbidden, a private errno adapter, and the original CPU-selection routine. All 206,228 inputs complete in each of three explicit CPU/precision modes. Initialized-SSE math substitution into the Mac generator matches all 110 MPFR-256 candidates. This is not complete Windows compiler/JVM execution. The image-default x87 candidate fails the unchanged startup-constant check; no complete-generator result is claimed for it.

Validation: 108 all-feature Rust tests, Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, six offline runtime guard tests, and original startup regression (26 initializers, 52 constants, 53 captured callbacks) pass. Private reports/outputs are ignored; canonical references and hardware locks are unchanged.

The user requires long-term self-contained Linux/macOS/Windows operation. Research MPFR/Linux/Apple helpers are not production dependencies. A controlled/versioned portable Rust math backend, historical Mac authentication, wider boundaries and complete Windows generator/JVM comparison remain pending. Do not close #5 or claim cross-platform/audio parity based on this milestone.

## Software-only Rust candidate follow-up

A separate optional helper evaluates pinned libm 0.2.16 with default features disabled and force-soft-floats enabled. The crate archive SHA-256 and all 155 archived files are verified, and Cargo must resolve that exact cached source/feature set with no transitive dependencies. The application manifest/backend remain unchanged.

All 206,228 observed inputs have identical debug/release results on Linux x86_64. Against MPFR-256, 996 results differ by at most one finite ULP. Substitution into the original Mac generator changes 96 of 110 packed outputs versus the canonical glibc adapter (266 words including checksums). The candidate is not adopted as a compatibility backend. Undefined-symbol checks find no imports of the tested host math functions, sqrt or FMA; the FFI helper itself still has normal OS runtime dependencies.

Three synthetic width/dispatch/signed-zero/domain/subnormal/profile regression tests, the six existing runtime guards, all 108 Rust tests, Clippy and formatting pass. Full Windows/macOS/other-architecture builds, complete Rust-engine substitution, controlled compatibility profiles and production dependency/source-preservation review remain pending. The v2 private audit report adds verified source/feature resolution and finite ULP measurements while preserving the initial report. #5 remains open.

A second strategy retains float32 inputs, evaluates those functions using the software float64 implementation and narrows results. All 203,217 observed float32 tuples now agree with MPFR-256; the 94 remaining differences are in double tan/pow/log (each one ULP). Debug/release agree across all 206,228 inputs per strategy. All 110 complete packed candidates match MPFR-256 and initialized Windows math. Wider intermediates do not guarantee correct rounding for arbitrary float32 arguments because of possible double rounding. Both strategies remain research-only; complete Rust-engine, broader and cross-target checks are pending. The first widened run saved outputs but failed writing its report due to a local variable collision; the corrected replay completed, preserving the earlier log/files.

## Experimental product profile implementation

The portable-math feature now selects software-wide-v1/libm-0.2.16 at build time; normal builds retain host-std-v1. The 44 coefficient math call sites use one Rust boundary, with a source guard and math-profile CLI identifier. The optional dependency is exact-pinned, architecture/intrinsic paths are disabled, and its license plus embedded source notices are preserved. No Linux math runtime or Line 6 runtime is required by this profile. This is experimental, not default rollout or hardware readiness.

Local evidence: all 110 tests and Clippy pass per profile. Actual host/software product debug and release binaries match 110 numeric cases and 48 synthetic-resource cases under corresponding original-instruction adapters. The software profile passes 144 original Java/native final preset-file comparisons in debug and release, including 24 special combinations; host replay preserves all 144 original references. Two special response snapshots are identical across profiles. Software CLI binaries import none of the tested host math functions.

Four initial generated-variant library tests failed the old host-math expectations (88/92 passed). A matching-profile original-instruction audit passes all 828 raw cases: 600 biquads, 64 pickup tables, 80 smoothed responses and 84 body interpolations. The 59 changed raw cases now have separate exact synthetic reference values; old fixtures are preserved and no tolerances added. These are existing inputs, not extra distinct-sample coverage for #33.

See docs/math-profiles.md and tests/fixtures/software-wide-v1/provenance.json. A pinned-compiler Offline core workflow is prepared for Ubuntu, Windows and macOS synthetic-only core/file tests; the software core/file matrix now passes 105 tests per debug/release target plus Clippy on Linux x86_64, Windows x86_64 and macOS ARM using Rust 1.99.1 (CI run 43753969448 on 6da3e45). Historical Mac authentication, full Windows compiler/JVM execution, broader parameter domains, profile/default rollout and audio safety remain open. Keep #5 open pending the remaining validation/disposition.

The first CI run exposed Windows debug CLI stack exhaustion and ARM NaN-sign differences in body interpolation/passive combinations. The CLI now uses an explicit 8 MiB command worker, and software math/computed combinations normalize NaNs to the reference negative quiet representation while preserving copied input payloads. Two new regression tests pass. Initial failed run 43752773871 is retained. Cross-target scope excludes GUI/USB integration and original assets; it is not audio/device safety proof.

## Integrated portable profile

PR #47 merged as dee5bdf2b907c242f4192f58f2569cd1d4940453. Final head 152597ca62905911cff24138ce7b8fabba79eaf6 passed Linux, Windows and macOS debug/release core tests and Clippy in run 43757929689. Default remains host-std-v1; software-wide-v1 is opt-in. Keep #5 open for historical-runtime authentication/full Windows runtime and default-rollout review; these do not block independent domain editing work in #7.

## Reviewed partial research milestone

PR #39 was revised after review and squash-merged at 818f5878b928367b274d82652a80050a4f509a0a. Issue #20 remains open: USB-firmware artifacts/applicable versions and the version-query protocol are not established, and the installed USB-component version remains unknown. PR #44 revised head df6a613678d8d60c96da90b4676df23aed5326b5 merged at 4aa4c12771fb598317d7363020dd85dcf7377393 after independent static review and 108 all-feature Rust tests, Clippy with warnings denied, and formatting. The POD device-manager construction is traced, but the returned service class is not established; the kernel and userspace version slots differ. This is a userspace-service candidate, not a confirmed end-to-end PODxt Live query.

The reviewer independently checked the request instructions, constructor trampoline and service forwarding, and the userspace/kernel vtable entries against the archived i386 executable. Its SHA-256 is recorded in docs/pod-usb-firmware.md. #20 remains open: actual service selection, firmware artifact, installed version, Windows confirmation and bcdDevice interpretation remain unresolved. Independent static review checked the description vtable slot and the control getter that returns cache index zero; all 108 all-feature tests, Clippy and formatting passed. This does not identify the cached class or establish a query. #20 remains open; no hardware access or sender was introduced.

Next offline scope: a bounded search for virtual setter assignments and cache initialization across available local libraries/exported callbacks. Absence of a direct call alone is not proof of a blocker. If that pass finds no additional offline edge, retain this gap and continue reserved issue #21. The recorded five fields remain unapproved for any live read.

## Reviewed setter/kernel-producer milestone

PR #48 revised head ef6d2a6523b3ae861f6675f33f593f6f105e813b merged at 0a5cc52 after independent 108 tests, Clippy/fmt, all nine recorded archive hashes, the description setter and the index-zero constructor path were checked. Class-name absence is a search observation and does not exclude stripped/different-ABI implementations. The kernel producer is not associated with the PODxt Live description yet; the userspace fields remain unselected and unapproved. #20 stays open with no sender or device access.

The next bounded offline edge search resolves Mach-O indirect/lazy-symbol bindings for setters and constructors in addition to direct calls, and checks factory/control association. No actual version, firmware artifact or recovery path is established by this milestone.

## Stub-binding and factory association

The bounded search resolved Mach-O indirect-symbol and lazy-symbol stubs for SetDeviceControl and the description and XT-audio constructors. Monkey and L6TWX_u.dylib have no symbol-table entry for the setter, so no stub binds its address. Line 6 License Manager and the L6MIDIJava i386 slice export the setter. Each has no direct PC-relative caller and no indirect-symbol entry.

In the Monkey image, USB PID 0x4650 at 0x953a6 allocates 0x418 bytes and calls 0x8c700 / 0x8c740, which stores vptr 0x1c18b8 (L6XTAudioControlMac). When control slot +0x18 returns with the failure bit clear, helper 0x95e10 calls description constructor wrapper 0x852f0 (body 0x85310, vptr 0x1c1598). The caller then loads slot +0x0c and calls setter 0x85650 with that control at 0x95616. License Manager names the same shape DriverAdded, GetDescription, and SetDeviceControl (compare 0xa6ee6, constructor 0x9df70, virtual call 0xa7156, setter 0x96ee0). The L6MIDIJava i386 slice has the same named shape (compare 0x2b0e6, constructor 0x22ebc, virtual call 0x2b28a, setter 0x1d8da). Those sibling addresses belong to their own images. License Manager's XT slot +0x0c is AcquireService; Monkey's control slot +0x0c remains the cache filler 0x8dd20.

The index-0 kernel service class remains unidentified, and that fill is not shown on this path. Missing class-name strings remain a search observation. The five recorded fields are not an approved live read. This pass found an additional offline edge, so reserved issue #21 was not started. #20 stays open. No USB-firmware image or installed version was established.

## AcquireService cache and kernel GetVersion

On the reviewed static success branch, the description control is L6XTAudioControlMac. Monkey 0x8dd20 matches License Manager L6XTAudioControlMac::AcquireService at 0x9f590. Those License addresses name the body. They are not Monkey addresses. A zero refcount at this+0x38 is a miss. Index 0 of the jump table is 0x8ddd0. It calls FindServiceNamed for com_line6_driver_sharedxt, allocates 0x10 bytes through the __Znwm stub at 0x169162, calls kernel constructor thunk 0x8ad80, and stores the pointer at this+8. The arm releases the named service through the _IOObjectRelease stub at 0x167a3a. The arm does not return the pointer.

The common epilogue calls 0x85150, the same body as L6DeviceControlBase::AcquireService. Index 0 of IsServiceSupported at 0x8cf5e sets the support bit with no product-id test. When the cached pointer is non-null, 0x85150 returns it and increments the refcount. A successful miss therefore returns the kernel service, vptr 0x1c1838. A hit returns the resident pointer and does not construct again. A null name leaves the slot null, and the base call returns null with status 0x80007301.

Kernel slot +0x14 at 0x8b810 calls 0x8b750 and then 0x88350. That call uses the _IOConnectCallScalarMethod stub at 0x1679b0 with selector 6, no scalar inputs, and an output count of 2, then the _sem_post stub at 0x169360. The semaphore helper at 0x8b360, called with 0x5dc, uses the _sem_trywait, ___error, and _usleep$UNIX2003 stubs. Those calls are indirect-symbol stubs. The kernel slot does not contain the userspace fields 0xC0, 0x67, and 0x0011. Those fields stay unapproved. This is not an observed device state. FindDriverService at 0x8e720 runs on the miss and its return is overwritten; its stores were not traced. The artifact and installed version remain unknown. #20 stays open. This pass found a further concrete edge, so #21 was not started.


## FindDriverService store and sharedxt selector 6

The AcquireService(0) miss calls FindDriverService and ignores its return. A UniqueID match stores a com_line6_audio registry entry at this+0x278. FindServiceNamed reads that word and returns the child named com_line6_driver_sharedxt. Sharedxt user-client externalMethod at 0x275f loads the service from user-client +0xd8 and supplies that object as the dispatch target. The selector-6 action at 0x2818 loads the target vtable and tail-calls slot +0x890 at 0x282f. The sharedxt vtable symbol is at 0xa8ec0, and the qword at 0xa9760 holds VersionStatusCommand at 0x13892. That tail-call is virtual. VersionStatusCommand builds the recorded five-field IOUSBDevRequest, and DeviceRequest at 0x141a6 and 0x141b2 forwards that pointer. Selector 7 is GetIOPVersion, a different method. The handler does not identify a firmware image. The five fields stay unapproved. This is not an observed device reply. The USB-firmware artifact and the installed version remain unknown. Issue #20 stays open. Issue #21 was not started because this edge is concrete.


Reviewed PR #54 merged as 0e01391134210c42e18bac2c4d9f7a695dc9810b, with independent 127-test/Clippy/fmt and three-platform core CI checks at revised head 31db9b91ef61f2cda8c9b1c7f186476d2333505a. The service-load branch additionally requires a null incoming dispatch target. Static request construction/forwarding is supported; artifact, installed version and authorization remain unresolved. See docs/pod-usb-firmware.md.

## USB interface callee is not archived

DeviceRequest stores the IOUSBInterface pointer at kusbinterface+0x10 and calls provider slot +0x8a8. The result is in RAX. 0x141a0 loads its vptr into R9, 0x141a3 passes that object as RDI, 0x141a6 passes the preserved request pointer, and 0x141b2 calls slot +0x978. The deleting destructor starts at 0x146c2. 0x146e0 is the size immediate 0x58 inside that function, and that size does not identify the object that receives the slot. The signed kext imports only IOUSBDevice, IOUSBInterface, and IOUSBControllerV2 metaClass symbols. No IOUSBFamily binary is in the local archive, so the callee body is not available and the three returned bytes stay uninterpreted. The display label and the five fields do not identify a firmware image. The fields stay unapproved. Issue #20 stays open on that limit. Reserved issue #21 follows it. No device was contacted.

- [ ] Track compatibility with JTV/HD Variax separately from PODxt/original Variax; no cross-flash, automatic conversion or live access.

## References

- `docs/product-vision.md`
- `README.md`
- `AGENTS.md`

Dependencies: #26.

## Hardware boundary

Offline work only. No USB/MIDI/audio streaming, device writes, reset, preset switching or firmware installation is authorized. Keep hardware disconnected and source locks enabled. Connecting audio equipment or starting capture/playback also requires separate explicit approval.

Backlog key: `hd500x`. Phase: `offline`.

items.title: Expand late-stage synthetic testing at least 5x, including sustain, bends and tuning
items.body:
Expand the offline test corpus toward the end of the initial Variax 600/PODxt Live application milestone, after the relevant implementations and simulator are ready. This is required before the readiness review; it does not authorize live tests. Apply the same policy to later device-family milestones.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record a versioned baseline per applicable suite (distinct cases, parameters, model/device coverage, fault classes, seed and runtime). Increase each selected suite to at least five times its baseline sample count; do not satisfy this by replaying identical inputs or inflating an aggregate with trivial cases.
- [ ] Expand coefficient/model pairings, wiring, tuning, boundary/invalid inputs, metadata/preset compatibility, simulated transport/update faults and synthetic recording streams where implemented. Correct and independently validate reference-oracle initialization before baselining it.
- [ ] Test continuous string bends: fractional/full-step bends and verified-range boundaries, onset/hold/release, vibrato, independent strings, unison bends and bent notes within chords. Use synthetic per-string audio trajectories rather than only changing stored tuning parameters.
- [ ] Test alternate/custom tunings (including drop/open patterns and DADGAD where representable), six independent string offsets, fractional detuning, string mix and relevant 12-string modes. Verify string numbering and bounds against original evidence.
- [ ] Combine bends/vibrato with alternate tuning, detuning, model changes and supported POD processing. Measure expected pitch trajectories, continuity, latency, artifacts, clipping and cross-string interactions against an independent reference where available.
- [ ] Distinguish settings/serialization/coefficient tests from actual audio/DSP behavior. Host-library emulation alone cannot prove string-bend tracking or sound equivalence. Unsupported audio or physical behaviors remain explicitly unverified, never counted as passed.
- [ ] Test sustain/note decay explicitly with synthetic per-string plucks and chords across bodies with differing decay characteristics, low/mid/high notes and varied input dynamics. Include long quiet tails, harmonic decay, body resonance and release/muting. Measure amplitude envelopes and decay times against independent body-specific references where available; do not normalize away intended sustain differences or count stored decay coefficients as audio proof. Detect premature cutoffs, gates/dropouts, pumping, instability, non-decaying output and residual noise. Combine bends/vibrato and alternate tuning with sustained notes and tails; test bend/hold/release during decay. Longer synthetic captures run offline without adding time to the short manual routine.
- [ ] Use deterministic seeds, unique-case deduplication, bounded execution, reproducible reports and meaningful failure diagnostics. Include longer-duration stream tests without opening an audio device.
- [ ] Reconcile README passes/pending/not-working and the readiness ledger. Keep all hardware disconnected and source locks enabled; final authorization remains a separate user decision.

## Dependencies and timing

After complete Rust/native coefficient validation (#6), offline receiver/update simulation (#18), initial-rig recording workflow (#28) and POD editor/library implementation (#29). Future HD-family expansions must satisfy their own equivalent late-stage test gate; they do not have to be completed to baseline the initial rig.

## Hardware boundary

No USB/MIDI/audio streaming, preset switching, resets, writes or firmware installation on real equipment. Use file-backed/synthetic audio, saved evidence, independent original-code references and in-memory emulation only. Passing this issue does not authorize connecting any device.


Audio scope clarification: the Variax 600 senses strings using piezo elements; Workbench pickups are virtual models. Do not count virtual-pickup coefficient parity as proof of piezo response, string tracking, sustain, bend tracking or physical pickup-height behavior. Model-specific decay/pitch expectations need independent audio/DSP evidence.

items.title: Add a short guided hardware and playing check with independent evidence
items.body:
Provide a short, guided Variax 600/PODxt Live commissioning workflow inside the unified Rust app, after the offline readiness review and explicit authorization. Target approximately five minutes; avoid requiring an entire fretboard sweep. The user should change the guitar's own controls while the app checks independent observations, then follow a few playing prompts.

## Current offline scaffold

`variax-check plan` displays five timed steps. `rehearse NEW_REPORT.txt` previews the workflow with equipment unplugged and records whether prompts are understood, problematic or skipped. It never reports hardware/audio passes and has no hardware or audio adapter. Report creation is atomic and refuses overwrite. This is an offline prototype, not completed recognition.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Integrate the short guided flow into the single application's UI: next/retry/skip/stop and a clear final report. Offer an optional longer neck sweep, never require it for the quick check.
- [ ] Establish which physical controls the protocol actually reports. Do not invent MIDI/USB telemetry or infer knob readings from loudness. Mark unsupported/unreported controls explicitly.
- [ ] Guide every model-selector position and pickup-switch position, then independent volume/tone sweeps with endpoint and midpoint checks. Correlate timestamped decoded observations to the user's declared choices; detect missed, duplicate, stale, out-of-order and wrong-control events.
- [ ] Confirm body/preset identity from decoded settings separately from physical switch selection. Stored presets may differ from factory settings.
- [ ] On a declared model/body and switch position, guide a short 18-note sample (six strings at open/fret 5/fret 12), then a bend/hold/release/vibrato sample. Compare expected versus measured pitch and flag dropouts/clipping or unavailable measurements. Do not assume mixed USB audio provides per-string telemetry.
- [ ] Optionally use an existing alternate-tuned preset: six open notes and one bend. Request actual per-string tuning; skip if unavailable. Never create/upload presets or trigger updates to satisfy this routine.
- [ ] Keep protocol evidence, measured audio results and user listening/visual observations distinct. A user clicking confirmation cannot become an automated recognition pass. Preserve raw evidence locally; incomplete, unsupported and skipped checks stay unverified.
- [ ] Verify workflow and correlation with synthetic missing/duplicate/stale control events and synthetic/file-backed audio before any live use. Future live control and audio adapters require the applicable offline gates plus explicit user authorization.
- [ ] Keep duration short; stop/cancel saves partial results without claims of automatic restoration. Record application/protocol version, settings, input source and timestamps in the final session report, without overwriting prior reports.

## Dependencies and safety

Full live integration depends on #24 (separately authorized staged reads) and #28 (audio/recording workflow), which themselves include the offline readiness gates. This issue is an additional manual commissioning check after those gates; it must not be a prerequisite of #22/#33, which would create a cycle.

The current hardware locks stay enabled. No live USB/MIDI/audio access, driver actions, writes, preset uploads, reset, bank switching by software or firmware installation is authorized. Future instructions to turn the guitar's physical controls apply only at the separately authorized session, not during offline rehearsal.

## Short sustain spot check

Include a brief listen-and-let-ring check on one low and one high note, ideally across two already available contrasting body presets. This replaces part of the existing note sample rather than adding a long sweep. Record the actual body/settings and audible tail/cutoff; measure decay only with independent captured evidence. Extensive body-by-body sustain and bending-during-decay testing belongs in the synthetic matrix #33.
